precedent_checks.what_is_contradicted: Per the CH paper (00-introduction.tex:113-124; 06-booleanization.tex:1-10, 343-358): Espindola 2023 Thm 4.1 is cited as claiming a categoricity transfer at the prescribed bound H(K) = beth_{(2^LS(K))^+} for arbitrary AECs. Theorem 1.1 (under CH) has the opposite conclusion at that bound, so (via Godel's L, where GCH and hence SCH also hold) Thm 4.1 cannot be a theorem of ZFC, or of ZFC+SCH, if ZFC is consistent. Section 7 pins the failing step: the proof starts from the full double-negation subtopos of presheaves on the countable internal-size site and asserts that a large categorical model gives a point of it; Prop bool:obstruction shows the canonical point p_H of any countable-base model (including every model of size >= Lambda) does not factor through Sh(C0^op, J_negneg), because the cosieve R_A of maps adding a base point is dense but not lifted inside H. The paper explicitly does not classify all points of the Booleanization or rule out other constructions of points. Search snippets confirm the paper's existence and that its abstract claims explicit thresholds and a ZFC classification of AEC categoricity spectra; the exact wording of Thm 4.1 could NOT be verified (arXiv/HAL unreachable).

Open: whether v7's proof uses the same double-negation canonical-point step that Section 7 obstructs.

candidates.name: Eventual reversal of strong maps via orbit-profile pigeonhole, two-size alignment and an omitting elimination chain
paper_items: with its gadgets EC-I09 (orbit names, arrow relation, profiles; 03-reversal.tex:404-422) and EC-I11 (alignment, 03-reversal.tex:509-554)
candidates.statement: For each theta there is b_K(theta) such that at every categoricity cardinal kappa >= b_K(theta), every strong self-map f of the kappa-model and every tuple a of length <= theta admit a strong g with g(f(a)) = a; no kappa^theta = kappa or cofinality hypothesis. Proof device: (i) profiles (named arrow relation + record->name map) range over a set of size <= 2^B independent of kappa, so among P^+ failing categoricity sizes two, a < mu with a^theta <= mu, share a profile; (ii) alignment: every <= a subset of the mu-model lies in a strong a-sized E(H(T)) whose theta-tuples have the same orbit names as in the big model; (iii) theta^+ rounds of an increasing chain of mu-models, enumerating the a^theta tuples of the current aligned small model and pushing each tuple whose orbit reaches p into orbit r (p -> r, not r -> p); the union A of the aligned small models is a copy of C_a omitting orbit p, contradiction. 'The small model supplies the alignment; the larger model accommodates the enumeration' (01-introduction.tex:221-224).

neighbours.ref: Shelah, Classification Theory for AECs (2009), Ch. IV, Claim IV.1.12 / Conclusion IV.2.14 (cited as Shelah2009 in EC bib)
neighbours.relation: Claims, for an AEC categorical in unboundedly many cardinals, that eventually <=_K coincides with L_{infty,LS^+}-elementarity; reversal of strong maps on short tuples in a categorical model follows from that claim. Same target statement (stronger form); the proof there needed an enumeration of theta-tuples in kappa steps.
neighbours.verdict: statement-level: stronger claimed version in L (with a known gap)

candidates.name: Return-tree split with a boundary-only accumulator (orbit counting in place of WGCH/weak diamond)
paper_items: EC-I25 proof of lem:iter:boundary-diagrams / thm:iter:boundary-completion (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/build/sections/09-marked-boundaries.tex:345-500, fig. iter:fig-return-tree)
candidates.statement: If a boundary map h of n-axis marked systems failed to preserve the type of a boundary tuple v over the base (witness f, diagrams delta0 != delta1), build branch worlds W_s for s in 2^{<=epsilon}, epsilon least with 2^epsilon > chi, splitting at each node into a Y^- copy and a Y^+ copy; keep full maps only along branches and only boundary maps q_s into a common accumulator A, identifying the two boundary copies of v. Completing the leaves gives 2^epsilon > chi orbits of f over <= chi parameters (v_s), contradicting the parameter orbit bound.

neighbours.relation: Identical cardinal bookkeeping (epsilon least with 2^epsilon > chi) and the same contradiction shape (too many types/orbits over a chi-sized parameter set against a stability/orbit bound).

family_D.lean_shortlist_consequence: None. The formalized manuscript (240-CH, OAI.CHObstruction.main) tops out at N2; EC-I12 and EC-I25 have no Lean and are not N3, so nothing goes to data/eureka_shortlist.json or data/eureka_informal.json from this family.
family_D.not_transfer: Set-theoretic tools (Erdos-Rado, Mostowski collapse, canonical functions, Fodor, Godel's L), Hahn-type ordered groups, F2 torsors and topos theory are N0 transfers; the candidates are the constructions built from them.
family_D.correctness_caveat: CH: text-level line-by-line check by the family analyst; Lean trusted as published (no build per project rule). EC: an unrefereed claim to resolve a central open problem with a competing prior claim (Espindola); Sections 5-9 and 11-13 read only at statement level; all EC grades are conditional on correctness.

provenance_flag.explanation: No cited work from 2025-2026 except the intra-family companion (240-CH, model-produced, same release), which EC cites for context only. The nearest external precedents (Espindola 2019-2023, Shelah-Vasey 2024/2018, Boney-Vasey 2015, Hart-Shelah 1990, KLH 2016, Saroch-Trlifaj 2023/24) are human-authored and pre-date model-produced research mathematics; no AI disclosure appears in any search snippet (abstract pages were not fetchable, so disclosure is unverified). Web searches for eventual categoricity with ChatGPT/GPT-5/OpenAI/AI-assisted found no model-produced precedent. Both manuscripts are model-produced (author 'OpenAI').

common.models: Training cutoff strictly before 2026-09-24 (the manuscripts' date; release 2026-10-06). Canary probes: ask for 'A CH obstruction to a prescribed categoricity threshold' and 'Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes' (openai/math) and whether Shelah's eventual categoricity conjecture has an accepted ZFC proof; exclude any model that recognises either manuscript. Exclude the OpenAI model(s) that produced family 240; run them only as an uncontrolled upper-reference arm. No browsing or tools. Judge model != proposer.
common.context_L: L = Mathlib d13f23b (ZFSet, Cardinal/Ordinal, beth, cof, DirectLimit) + the CH bib (14) and EC bib (20) minus OpenAI2026CHThreshold, given as abstracts plus the invoked statements. Espindola 2019/2023 stay in L (they contain none of the candidates); an arm without them measures their effect.
common.sampling: n = 256 samples per arm, temperature 1.0, fixed reasoning budget (32k tokens); unbiased pass@k for k in {1,2,4,...,256}.
common.judging: Two independent LLM judges with the paper's precedent remarks and this file's neighbour lists in the prompt; an AEC model theorist checks all hits and 10% of misses. P-C3 can additionally be judged in Lean.
common.controls: Positive: Cook-Reckhow ER extension variables for PHP. Negatives: EC-I14 (closure-point back-and-forth) and CH-I19 (partition-estimate tail bound) in the same format.

P-C1.lean: no (informal LLM-judge protocol; informal list rules)
P-C1.hide: EC-I09, EC-I11, EC-I12 and everything downstream (EC Sections 4-14).
P-C1.give: EC Sections 2-3 up to the uniform orbit bound (EC-I01..I08, I10), the statement of Theorem found:reversal as the target, and Boney-Vasey 2015's description of the Ch. IV gap.

arms.directed: target statement given; ask for a proof
arms.open: ask only for a ZFC lemma making strong maps symmetric at large categoricity cardinals of arbitrary cofinality

P-C1.equivalence: Hit: a proof that (a) uses two categoricity sizes a < mu with a^theta <= mu sharing an orbit invariant, and (b) builds a chain whose union is a copy of the small categorical model omitting a realized orbit. Partial: (b) alone with a kappa^theta = kappa assumption (that is the known route).

P-C2.hide: The proof of Lemma iter:boundary-diagrams / Theorem iter:boundary-completion and EC-I26, I30, I33 downstream.
P-C2.give: All statements of EC Sections 2-9 before it, including the parameter orbit bound (calc:parameter-orbits) and lower-dimensional completion; target = Lemma iter:boundary-diagrams.

arms.baseline: target given with WGCH allowed (expect the weak-diamond count)

P-C2.equivalence: Hit: a binary tree of height epsilon (2^{<epsilon} <= chi < 2^epsilon) of competing amalgams in which only boundary maps are kept coherent in a shared accumulator, closed by an orbit/type count over <= chi parameters. Partial: a generic 'many types' tree that does not resolve the cross-face equality issue.

P-C3.hide: Data.IsObject, Map.Strong, classData and everything downstream (AEC.isAEC, EndpointModels.twoModels, Categoricity.tail, Main).
P-C3.give: Problem: under CH, an AEC with LS = aleph_0, two models at beth_{omega2}, categorical from beth_{(2^aleph1)^+}. Plus Colors/Diagrams/Tests (CH-I01..I05), Arrays.Data without IsObject, and Hart-Shelah/KLH abstracts.
P-C3.equivalence: Hit: objects allow a small (countable / < LS^+) exceptional set of base points per index tuple, while strong extensions require exact test satisfaction at all new base points. Lean check: the proposed class satisfies isAEC and plugs into twoModels/index_lt with the released proofs adapted.

Prior art for the CH headline itself: is any AEC known (in ZFC or under extra axioms) that is categorical on a tail but not at H(K)? Searches found Hanf-number lower bounds for amalgamation/JEP/stability (KLH 2016, Baldwin-Boney, Leung 2108.00565) but no categoricity-at-H(K) counterexample.
